key_insight: Porting the AHBR range-separated hybrid vdW-DF functional from Quantum Espresso to VASP enables stable stress-based unit-cell optimization for complex-matter structure prediction.
engineering_relevance: This makes high-accuracy DFT more practical for discovering and refining atomic structures in soft, layered, magnetic, and weakly bound materials.
method: Implemented the AHBR XC functional in VASP to support robust stress-driven geometry optimization.
Compared AHBR-VASP against AHBR-QE for molecular non-covalent interactions and bulk cohesion/structure.
Applied the new implementation to distorted-rocksalt metal monoxides and C2N COF layer-stacking motifs.
evidence_signal: The implementation was validated by cross-code comparisons on molecular interactions and simple bulk systems, then demonstrated on representative complex materials problems.
watch_item: The main concern is implementation portability and stability: stress-based optimization was not robust in the original QE setup, so results still depend on careful code-specific validation.
paper_title: Stress-based structure optimization for a range-separated hybrid van der Waals density functional
